video_title: Rich Paul x Max On Clippers’ BRUTAL Punishment

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' loss of five first-round picks for salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: How do you expect them to be competitive? The point of the salary cap is to stop ourselves.
quotes.quote: You're taking five first-round picks away from them. Five first-round picks. How do you expect them to be competitive? The point of the salary cap is to stop ourselves from paying the players what they're worth. Meaning, if we took the handcuffs off and we could all bid on the players, we know ourselves, and some of us would bid the price higher. And so in order to stop some of us who are competitive and maybe deeper pocketed from bidding the price higher, we curb our ability to even do that with a rule that says we can't do that. That's all a salary cap is.

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' path to competitiveness without first-round draft picks
quotes.excerpt: How do they stay competitive? You got to put your head down and keep marching.

text_blocks.speaker: Max Kellerman
text_blocks.text: How do you do if you're the Clippers now? How do they stay competitive?

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Paul
text_blocks.text: You got to put your head down and keep marching. That's all you can do.

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of building a team without draft assets
quotes.excerpt: But what do you do to build the team? Obviously, it's going to be much harder.

text_blocks.speaker: Max Kellerman
text_blocks.text: But what do you do to build the team? Obviously, it's going to be much harder to circumvent the salary cap.

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Paul
text_blocks.text: I don't know. I mean, it's a touchy subject for me. Obviously, I have several clients on the team, so I just think you just got to put your head down and keep pushing.

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: Rich Paul's assessment of the current Clippers roster competitiveness
quotes.excerpt: Do you think they have enough to be competitive right now? Yes, I do.

text_blocks.speaker: Max Kellerman
text_blocks.text: Do you think they have enough to be competitive right now?

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential strategies for the Clippers to acquire future draft assets
quotes.excerpt: Do you look to trade assets to gain first-round picks going forward? I don't know.

text_blocks.speaker: Max Kellerman
text_blocks.text: Do you look to trade assets to gain first-round picks going forward? Do you look to red paper clip it where you trade something for something else of relatively equal value, but it fills a need for the other person so they give you a little extra value? And then you keep doing that till you have something more valuable?

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Paul
text_blocks.text: I don't know. I'm going to leave that up to somebody else to play GM. I don't want to play fantasy GM for that team. But my advice to my guys is just, hey, just keep your head down and keep grinding.

quotes.speaker: Max Kellerman
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green's concerns regarding the redistribution of forfeited draft picks
quotes.excerpt: Draymond Green brought up an interesting point, which is what happens to those first-rounders?

text_blocks.speaker: Max Kellerman
text_blocks.text: One of your clients, by the way, Draymond Green, brought up an interesting point, which is what happens to those first-rounders? Because the first round, you have your contract guaranteed. So those first-round picks that the Clippers forfeit, shouldn't they be redistributed to another team so that you have 30 picks in the first round?

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Paul
text_blocks.text: Well, I think 58 players drafted for the last three, four years, so we've been missing two anyway.
